scientific_findings: The hidden quantum state is retained through drive changes; filtering sums source paths before applying each measurement instrument.
Inference receives observed bits and frozen calibrated model/schedule priors, not latent true schedules or nuisance onset. Truth is used only for held-out scoring.
Base instrument flags include dark counts; added afterpulse-only flags retain the underlying trajectory; blind bins use the full channel.
At this budget prompt source-change detection is weak; the nominal 20 percent step yields 19 of 512 physical-model detections within 32 bins.
Several drive-estimation RMSEs improve over the fitted constant baseline, while stable-source controls incur nonzero positive amplitude estimates.
Detector dark-count/afterpulse changes induce false source alarms; these are model-mismatch failures, not recovered causes.
limits: All inference and data generation are classical local simulation of a finite quantum model. No physical laser, QPU, wavelength compatibility, wafer yield, dollar savings, or quantum advantage validated.
Four pipelines share fixed nominal physical parameters and use idealized finite detector calibration; nuisance parameters are not jointly identified.
The physical model has correct-family prior information and extra calibration; this is not a resource-matched optical receiver contest.
The evaluated source alternatives increase drive only. Conditional posterior means do not uniquely diagnose a real cause.
Hierarchical percentile interval coverage is uncalibrated, especially with four calibration clusters; numerical means and denominators were audited, not statistical coverage.
Cavity 4 versus 5 marginal differences are a sensitivity check, not proof of infinite-cutoff convergence.
